3.text: 60 kopeks; in Sredne-Kolymsk, 1.80 rubles; at the Anui fair, 2.40 rubles or

4.text: 3 black fawn-skins of small size; in Anadyr, 80 kopeks; on the tundra, 5

5.text: black fawns-kins; in the Chukchee Peninsula, 1 white-fox skin.

6.text: In Vladivostok or Irkutsk a piece of brick-tea is worth about 30 kopeks;

7.text: in Yakutsk, 50 kopeks; in Sredne-Kolymsk and on the tundra it is equivalent

8.text: to a bundle of tobacco. One Russian pound (nine-tenths of a pound Avoir-

9.text: dupois) of sugar is worth in southern Russia 15 kopeks; in Yakutsk, 40 kopeks;

10.text: in Sredne-Kolymsk, 1 ruble; at the Anui fair, 1.50 rubles or 2 black and 1

11.text: gray fawn-skin of the smaller size.

12.text: A bottle of undiluted alcohol is worth, in Sredne-Kolymsk, from 2 to 2.50

13.text: rubles; at the Anui fair (largely diluted with water), 5 rubles or a good red-

14.text: fox skin; on the tundra and in the Anadyr, any price that it will bring.

15.text: In trading with the whalers, a storehouse that is worth $100 in San

16.text: Francisco, is sold for 100 slabs of whalebone (about 400 pounds), worth from

17.text: $2.50 to $3.50 per pound; i. e., for $1000-$1400. A second-hand whale-

18.text: boat, with equipment, is sold for 20-30 slabs of whalebone, or from $200 to

19.text: $420; a shotgun or a Winchester rifle with reloading-tools, for 4-6 slabs; a

20.text: small box of chewing-tobacco (6¼ pounds), for 2 pairs of boots; a keg of black

21.text: molasses, for 1 or 2 pairs of boots; a sack of white flour, for 1 or 2 pairs

22.text: of boots; etc. A good fawn-skin is equal in value to a pair of boots; a plain

23.text: garment, to 2 pairs of boots; an embroidered garment, to a slab of whale-

25.text: At the mouth of the Anadyr, American wares are bartered away by the

26.text: Chukchee for commodities that, according to our scale of prices, are worth

27.text: less than what is paid to the whalers for them. One rifle is sold for from

28.text: 20 to 30 pieces of brick-tea, i. e., 8 to 12 rubles; one whale-boat, for 70

29.text: pieces of brick-tea, 30 pounds of sugar, 20 pounds of tobacco. — in all, about

30.text: 50 rubles. Smaller articles, such as powder, percussion-caps, cotton goods,

31.text: are bought by the Cossacks at still cheaper rates. The reason is, that in

32.text: former times the Russians did not accept whalebone, and set on their wares

33.text: high prices in peltries; so that the Maritime natives who barter at present

34.text: for American wares with whalebone are accustomed to regard them as of

35.text: lesser value in comparison with Russian wares.

36.text: In the inland trade among the western camps, prices are as follows: for

37.text: a hide of a large ground-seal, from 10 to 15 fawn-skins of larger size; for a

38.text: coil of white thong, 5 fawn-skins; for a large bag full of seal-oil, 3 reindeer

39.text: for slaughter; for a Winchester rifle with accessories, 2 sledge-reindeer; etc.

40.text: Among the Kerek a Winchester rifle with accessories is worth 2 sable-skins.
